To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) keyphrases from different sources are complementary to each other and can improve the quality of query suggestion generation; and (2) query suggestions can help improve the performance of task-oriented search.

(i) our model is effective for generating task-oriented query suggestions, (ii) the keyphrases obtained from multiple sources complement each other, and (iii) the quality of the keyphrases is crucial for generating high-quality query suggestions.
(a) keyphrase generation from multiple sources is a promising approach for generating query suggestions, and (b) the combination of different sources is beneficial.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are able to generate query suggestions which cover the underlying task of the query with a precision of 50% and a coverage of 70%.
our model outperforms all the baselines in terms of precision, recall and F1 score.
the best query suggestion model is a simple combination of keyphrase generation and query generation, with a small number of keyphrases (5-10), which is also the simplest model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can obtain keyphrases for a given query with high precision and that our query suggestion generator can provide good suggestions.
we can generate task-based query suggestions that are useful for the user.
we have a good coverage for the task-based search, but we need more training data to improve the quality of suggestions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of keyphrases extracted from multiple sources (including Wikipedia, webpages, and query logs) provides the most effective suggestions for the task-based search task.

a simple model based on keyphrases can be used to generate query suggestions that are relevant to the underlying task and are able to cover a significant part of the relevant documents in the search engine.
we can generate query suggestions that are useful in the context of a user’s task, which in turn can be used to improve the performance of task-based search systems.
